newsitem.title: UK: Ldn freight features mostly Pacific business.
newsitem.headline: Ldn freight features mostly Pacific business.

text.p: London's freight trade remained muted on Friday and rates broadly unchanged but some shipbrokers said the market was at a crossroads, especially in the benchmark USGulf/Japan route.
The key Panamax run featured no new deals after the last fixture at $23 basis no combination, but brokers said the price could be on the brink of a hike due to seasonal demand factors.
"We may see it moving up again next week," said one.
Panamax brokers reported more grain enquiries in the Pacific while Atlantic business remained quiet. Friday's reported deals consisted almost entirely of Pacific timecharter fixtures.

These included Akra Tairanon 69,600 dwt by HMM delivery Japan early Dec for three to five months trading at $10,500 daily, Yu May 65,000 dwt delivery Japan early Dec for Pacific round at $11,000 daily and 1983 built Baia de Arama 64,879 dwt delivery USGulf Dec 10/20 trip redelivery Korea $10,250 daily plus $200,000 bonus HMM.
Brokers said South African traders were testing the water for possible coal shipments to the Mediterannean but no fixtures have yet surfaced.
Capers were also weaker in the Atlantic while prompt positions in the Pacific commanded higher rates.

One broker said Trans-pacific timecharter rates for December were running in the region of $13,000-$14,000 a day as opposed to $12,000 for January dates. Forward rates were softer due to concerns of heavy shipbuilding.

Brokers said a tender by Korean Posco for 140,000-200,000 tonnes iron ore from Seven Islands to Qwang Yeng and/or Pohang was awarded to Cho Yang for January 11-25 at a shade over $11 -- which they said was quite low.
The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) remained unchanged on Friday at 1,423 points while nearby BIFFEX futures contracts were up 18 points with December at 1,400 and January at 1,360.
